static_traits.name: Chen Kai
static_traits.family_status: Lives alone in Las Vegas, Nevada, USA
static_traits.social_status: Having a few friends to chat with, but not yet discussing one's sense of incompetence with them; relationship with a fellow fishing-loving friend affected by one's Persistent self-doubt and comparison
static_traits.medical_history: No history of similar psychological problems; has not received psychotherapy; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, strong logic, open and cooperative, able to self-Reflect; Positive attitude

basic_info.main_problem: I constantly feel I must be terrible at fishing, because my catch never measures up to professional anglers' catches, which makes me feel incompetent and inferior, gradually affecting my confidence in other abilities.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize these feelings of incompetence are affecting my self-esteem and enjoyment of the hobby, which prompted me to seek counseling.
growth_experiences: Started fishing as a hobby a few years ago. Every weekend fishing trip, comparing one's catch with professional anglers, feeling one must reach professional level, otherwise being a failure. This comparison and self-reproach gradually Reinforced the belief 'I am terrible/I am not capable', destroying the weekend relaxation experience and further spreading to doubts about other abilities. To improve performance, tried watching tutorials, changing fishing spots and techniques, but the sense of inferiority persisted.

core_beliefs: If I cannot reach professional level, I am a failure

special_situations.event: Goes fishing on the weekend and compares the catch with professional anglers
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I catch less than them, it proves I am terrible, I failed
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly comparing and doubling efforts: watching tutorials, changing fishing spots, using different techniques to 'prove oneself'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them/I must be terrible

special_situations.event: Anticipating one's performance before or during fishing trips
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not catch many fish this time, it means I will never get better
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sets overly high standards, excessive tension and self-pressure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never get better at this

special_situations.event: Recalling fishing outings that were once rewarding
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Even good performance does not represent ability; success is just luck
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive experiences, attributing success to outside accidental factors
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: That time was just good luck, not my skill

special_situations.event: Interacts with friends (who also like fishing) or talks about fishing results
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I fish worse than them, they will look down on me, showing I am not capable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces communication, avoids talking about feelings to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am terrible

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized as capable and accepted in front of significant others (friends/fellow enthusiasts)
core_conflict.fear: Fears being seen as a failure, compared and belittled; worries about losing self-esteem and sense of value
defense_goal: Avoiding shame and being negated by maintaining extremely high standards and self-reproach, maintaining the 'incompetent' self-schema by negating positive experiences to control uncertainty

object_relations.self_representation: A lesser-than-others failure who needs to constantly prove oneself

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others invite him to review successful fishing experiences and look for evidence of ability
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understanding success as an accident, insufficient to prove one's ability (tending to negate the positive)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Calm, somewhat objectifying tone, emphasizing 'luck/outside factors', downplaying skill and effort, giving 'but/however' style responses to positive feedback.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing goal setting and standards (such as suggesting setting more realistic expectations)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Automatically taking professional level as the only acceptable standard, uncritically adopting outside high standards as self-rules
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using 'should/must' phrasing, insisting on professional level as the benchmark, showing hesitation or mild resistance toward more flexible goals.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about interactions with fishing buddies and others' evaluations
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Attributing one's own shame and inferiority experiences to others' 'looking down on me' attitude (Projection)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: States others' negative views in a cautious tone, emphasizes others' possible judgment, avoids exploring their own feelings in depth.

manifestations: Fishing, originally done for relaxation, has been 'spoiled' by constant comparison and self-reproach; the weekend experience is ruined, and they gradually doubt their own ability and worth
outcomes: Worsening subjective sense of incompetence and inferiority
Loss of enjoyment in leisure and hobbies
Confusion about and devaluation of self-worth

manifestations: Tense relationship with fellow hobbyist friends due to Self-doubt and comparison; not discussing true feelings with friends

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeatedly self-evaluating in sessions as 'I am terrible/I am not capable'
Attributing success to luck and denying one's own skill
Sets excessively high and rigid performance standards for oneself

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Takes professional standards as the only qualifying bar
Hard to accept more flexible, experience-centered goals

exception_events.target_problem: When fishing on weekends, the client usually compares with professional anglers and develops strong Self-denial, leading to Depression, ruined weekend experiences, Tense relationships with friends.
exception_events.unique_outcome: On some fishing days actually catching fish and briefly feeling Good and more confident (not completely sinking into the sense of failure as before), sensing the positive side of the experience.
exception_events.reason: Clues: possibly because the location, equipment, or weather was more suitable, or different techniques were tried; these outside and strategic factors made that experience deviate from the past with positive results.

positive_force: Positive attitude, willing to explore a more balanced perspective
Has willingness to act and learn (watches tutorials, changes fishing spots, tries techniques)
Still retaining certain positive experiences and success evidence (having caught fish before)
Has some friend resources (can seek support)
negative_force: Excessively compares with professional standards and judges oneself by them
Cognitive tendencies toward black-and-white thinking and overgeneralization
Negating positive experiences (attributing success to luck)
Predicting failure, persistent self-reproach, leading to Decreased self-esteem

target_behavior.behavior: Strong Self-denial and sense of incompetence in weekend fishing situations (negative Automatic thoughts and self-deprecating speech)
antecedent: Fishing on weekends and seeing one's catch fall short of professional anglers
Watching tutorials or videos of professional anglers
Chatting or comparing catches with fishing buddies
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalizing professional level as the only judging standard, catastrophically and absolutely evaluating one's performance, forming the stable self-schema of 'I am terrible/I am not capable'
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the Anxiety of failure and being negated, maintaining a controllable Interpretation framework through self-criticism (Self-protection), while reducing contact with uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Weekend relaxation and enjoyment ruined, Decreased self-esteem; Interpersonal tension; doubts about abilities in other areas
